questions.q: What is a container registry, according to this lesson?
options: A server that stores images, organized into named repositories with tagged versions
A text file listing every container running on a machine
A Dockerfile instruction
A tool for writing Python dependencies
questions.explain: A registry stores images (not running containers) in repositories, each with one or more tags — Docker Hub by default, or a private registry from AWS, GCP, Azure, or GitHub.

questions.q: In the reference `ghcr.io/yourname/my-ai-app:latest`, what does leaving out the registry host entirely (as in `yourname/my-ai-app:1.0`) tell Docker?
options: That the image cannot be pushed anywhere
To use the local filesystem instead of a registry
To automatically pick the fastest available registry
To assume Docker Hub
questions.explain: Docker Hub is the default registry when no host is specified in an image reference.

questions.q: Why is `latest` a risky tag to rely on for reproducibility, per this lesson?
options: It's reserved and cannot actually be pushed to
It only works with private repositories
It's an ordinary, overwritable tag — just whatever was last pushed without an explicit version
It always points to the oldest version of an image
questions.explain: `latest` isn't a special guarantee — it's an ordinary tag that gets reassigned to whatever is pushed next without an explicit version.

questions.q: What does `docker tag my-ai-app:1.0 yourname/my-ai-app:1.0` actually do?
options: Adds a second, registry-shaped name to the same local image — it doesn't copy or upload anything
Uploads the image's layers to a registry
Deletes the original local image
Builds a brand new image from scratch
questions.explain: docker tag renames/aliases an existing local image; docker push is the separate step that actually uploads it.

questions.q: On Docker Hub's "Create a repository" form shown in this lesson, what does choosing Private vs. Public control?
options: The number of tags a repository can have
Whether the repository is searchable and pullable by anyone, or restricted to your account/organization
Whether the image can be built with a Dockerfile
The maximum size of the image
questions.explain: Public repositories are searchable and pullable by anyone; Private restricts access to your account or organization — relevant for images that embed model weights or secrets.
